addressForm: siz (polite plural) in sentences for operators and customers; buttons as the short verb stem (Sifariş et, Yadda saxla). Evidence: Bolt Food AZ addresses businesses with siz (“Sadəcə ünvanınızı daxil edin”, “Siz diqqətinizi biznesinizə cəmləyin”) but customers with sən (“Onlayn sifariş et”, “Sifarişini izlə”); HatchGrab writes as a business tool, so siz throughout, never sən in sentences.

WebSearch “restoran avtomatlaşdırma POS sistemi kassa proqramı …” — lalafo.az ads for R-Keeper/TamPos/UniPOS restaurant POS bundles, “KASSA DƏSTİ”, kassa avadanlığı
en.wikipedia langlinks API — az titles: “Küçə yeməyi” (Street food), “Ketrinq” (Catering), “Satış nöqtəsi” (Point of sale, literal); no az article for Food truck
WebSearch “food truck … Bakı küçə yeməkləri festival” — azernews.az: Baku Street Food Festival (İçərişəhər, 2017), Summer Food Fest, Food and Drinks Fest; no Azerbaijani food-truck term surfaced
confidence: Low-Med — siz/sən split, “Al-apar”, “Sifarişi planlaşdır”, menyu, kombo, kassa/POS and küçə yeməyi are confirmed on Bolt/Wolt AZ, lalafo.az and Wikipedia; the food-truck word itself (Latin “food truck”), “özün götür”, “götürmə vaxtı”, Pay at Hatch and plan names rest on general Azerbaijani usage. csvRows are what WebSearch (US-indexed) returned for “food truck onlayn sifariş sistemi Azərbaycan”, not a local Google SERP; no Azerbaijani food-truck ordering vendor surfaced.
decisions: Food-truck word: recommend the Latin loanword “food truck” (plural “food truck-lar”, suffixes after a hyphen as Azerbaijani writes WhatsApp-da, Wolt-da); alternatives “yemək maşını” / “səyyar kafe” found no usage in the research. Native check advised.
Address form: siz in all sentences (operator and customer); Bolt uses sən for consumers, but a mixed register inside one product reads badly. Buttons: verb stem (“Sifariş et”, “Yadda saxla”).
Pay at Hatch: “Götürərkən ödəniş” (feature) / “Yerində ödəniş” (short). Never “qapıda ödəniş”, “çatdırılma zamanı ödəniş” or “kuryerə nağd” (delivery wording).
Pickup: “özün götür” for the collect option, “al-apar” (Bolt’s word) for takeaway in general; Wolt’s word for its pickup mode was not visible (pages render client-side).
Order button: no statutory button wording was found for Azerbaijan (the consumer-rights and e-commerce law texts were not fetched); market norm “Sifariş et” / “Sifarişi təsdiqlə”.
WhatsApp is widely used in Azerbaijan, so the WhatsApp auto-reply feature can stay prominent.
